story.title: Typhoon Dolphin Triggers Mass Evacuations in Eastern China
story.summary: Typhoon Dolphin has made landfall in eastern China, prompting the evacuation of over one million residents. The storm has brought heavy rain and strong winds, leading to significant disruptions, including the cancellation of nearly 1,000 flights in Shanghai. Authorities have issued top-level alerts as the storm is expected to move further inland in the coming days.

event_overview.title: About Typhoon Dolphin
event_overview.subject: Typhoon Dolphin
event_overview.summary: Typhoon Dolphin was the 13th named tropical cyclone of the 2026 western North Pacific season, forming in late July and later tracking westward across the region. It affected Japan’s Okinawa area before making landfall in Zhejiang province on China’s east coast; by August 10 it had weakened to a tropical storm inland.

facts.label: Formation and designation
facts.value: China’s National Meteorological Center designated Dolphin as 2026’s No. 13 typhoon; official reporting said it formed over the northwestern Pacific on July 27, 2026.

facts.label: China landfall and weakening
facts.value: Dolphin made landfall near Taizhou, Zhejiang, on the evening of August 9 with reported winds of 151 kph; on August 10, China’s National Meteorological Center listed it as a tropical storm over Dexing, Jiangxi, and forecast further weakening.

facts.label: Naming system
facts.value: “Dolphin” is a name contributed by Hong Kong, China, under the ESCAP/WMO Typhoon Committee naming list; it refers to the Chinese white dolphin and a Hong Kong mascot.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the August 8-10 Japan-to-China impact period and preparedness or disruption measures, not Dolphin’s full late-July development, its complete inland dissipation, or all effects elsewhere in the region.

explore_lenses.label: What changed after landfall?
explore_lenses.title: The storm weakened, but flooding risks persisted
explore_lenses.summary: By August 10, Dolphin had weakened from a typhoon to a tropical storm and moved inland into Jiangxi, while authorities reported localized flooding and continued warnings about flood and landslide hazards.

claims.text: China's National Meteorological Center listed Dolphin at 20 m/s (about 72 km/h) at 19:00 on August 10, located in Dexing, Jiangxi province.
The Associated Press reported flooding in parts of eastern China, with Yueqing authorities searching flooded homes and clearing storm debris.
The China Meteorological Administration forecast that Dolphin would continue moving northwest at 15-20 km/h and weaken until it dissipates.

The Associated Press reported flooding in parts of eastern China, with Yueqing authorities searching flooded homes and clearing storm debris.
The China Meteorological Administration forecast that Dolphin would continue moving northwest at 15-20 km/h and weaken until it dissipates.

explore_lenses.label: How did evacuations and shutdowns build?
explore_lenses.title: Authorities acted before the coast was hit
explore_lenses.summary: The large-scale disruption was driven chiefly by precautionary measures before landfall, including evacuations from risk areas, transport suspensions, school closures, and restrictions on maritime activity.

claims.text: Before landfall, authorities relocated more than 300,000 people, including about 390,000 reported evacuated in Taizhou and more than 30,000 from higher-risk areas of Shanghai; these figures indicate that counts reported at different stages and locations were not directly comparable.
Shanghai's two airports canceled more than 1,300 flights, while Zhejiang authorities suspended ferries and cruises.
Ahead of landfall, Ningbo closed schools and halted water-related activities, and tourist destinations across Zhejiang shut or suspended operations.

explore_lenses.label: What are the next operational risks?
explore_lenses.title: Attention shifts inland to rain-driven hazards
explore_lenses.summary: With Dolphin now inland and weaker, the immediate operational concern is no longer peak coastal wind but heavy-rain impacts, including urban flooding, landslides, and the pace at which transport and local services can safely resume.

claims.text: At landfall in Taizhou, Zhejiang, Dolphin had winds of about 151 km/h; forecasters warned that 200-400 mm of rain could fall in affected areas over the following days.
Authorities warned of severe flooding and landslide risks after landfall.
The National Meteorological Center forecast at 19:00 on August 10 that Dolphin would move west-northwest at about 15 km/h and gradually weaken.

story_report.summary: Typhoon Dolphin made landfall in eastern China at Taizhou, Zhejiang, with winds of about 151 km/h, bringing heavy rain, strong winds and warnings of severe flooding and landslides. Contemporaneous reports said more than one million people were evacuated as authorities moved residents from vulnerable areas. The storm also disrupted travel, with Shanghai airport cancellations reported in the hundreds and more than 1,300 flights later cited across the city’s two airports.

sections.heading: Transport and Services Face Disruption
sections.body: Shanghai’s two airports canceled more than 1,300 flights, while authorities in Zhejiang suspended ferries and cruises. Ningbo closed schools and halted water-related activities before landfall, and tourist destinations across Zhejiang shut or suspended operations. The consulted sources did not give a confirmed timetable for restoring flights, ferry services, schools or tourism operations.

sections.heading: Dolphin Weakens on Inland Track
sections.body: At 19:00 on August 10, China’s National Meteorological Center listed Dolphin in Dexing, Jiangxi province, with sustained winds of 20 metres per second, or about 72 km/h. The agency forecast that the storm would continue northwest or west-northwest at roughly 15-20 km/h, gradually weaken and eventually dissipate.

sections.heading: Local Evacuations Preceded Landfall
sections.body: Before landfall, authorities reported relocating more than 300,000 people, including about 390,000 evacuees in Taizhou and more than 30,000 people from higher-risk parts of Shanghai. The reported figures were compiled at different stages and locations, meaning they are not directly comparable. Flooding was reported in parts of eastern China, where Yueqing authorities searched flooded homes and cleared storm debris.

unresolved.text: A single official total for evacuations was not identified: while some contemporaneous reports put the number above one million, consulted AP reports provided lower, location-specific counts.
The consulted sources did not identify a consolidated official toll for casualties, damage or people who remained displaced.

related_stories.title: Syria Regains Control of Key Mediterranean Bases from Russia
related_stories.summary: Syria and Russia have reached an agreement that allows Syria to regain control of two strategic Mediterranean bases: the Hmeimem air base and part of Tartous port. The deal, announced by Syria's foreign ministry, stipulates that the remaining military facilities will be transformed into joint training centers.

related_stories.title: Deadly Ukrainian Drone Attack in Russia Claims 13 Lives
related_stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack on the industrial city of Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan has resulted in at least 13 fatalities and numerous injuries. This incident marks one of the deadliest strikes on Russian territory since the onset of the conflict. Reports indicate that the attack targeted industrial and civilian sites, with local authorities confirming the casualties and injuries.
